counterevidence_considered.description: Potential concern: all 24 pots share one soil batch and one watering schedule, which could be read as a shared-environment dependence. Checked and rejected as an instance of this issue class: shared conditions do not constitute repeated entry of the same authorized independent unit into the row-independent procedure; each pot still contributes exactly one row and one table entry.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: shared soil batch and watering schedule; each pot still entered once

source_refs.quoted_text:
Twenty-four nursery pots were filled from one batch of screened field soil, and
each pot received exactly one sulphur buckwheat (Eriogonum umbellatum) seed.
Every seed came from a different wild maternal plant, so no maternal plant is

evidence.description: The input CSV contains exactly 24 data rows with 24 distinct pot_id values (P01 through P24) and 24 distinct maternal_plant_id values (M01 through M24); no independent unit appears more than once.

The workflow explicitly enforces at-most-one row per pot and per maternal plant before any statistics are computed, raising an error on any duplicate, so a repeated independent-unit entry cannot silently reach the Fisher test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate pot_id or maternal_plant_id raises ValueError before analysis

evidence.description: The reported 2x2 counts match a manual tally of the CSV (pelleted 9 emerged / 3 not; bare 3 emerged / 9 not; 24 pots total), and the reported two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.0391 and odds ratio 9.00 match a manual hypergeometric recomputation (2 * 52901 / 2704156 = 0.03912), confirming each unit entered the row-independent procedure exactly once.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Two-sided Fisher's exact test on 24 independent single-seed pots: emergence 9/12 (75.0%) with pelleted seed vs. 3/12 (25.0%) with bare seed, sample odds ratio 9.00, p = 0.0391; the difference is statistically significant at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by (1) scanning all 24 CSV data rows for any duplicated pot_id or maternal_plant_id (none: P01-P24 and M01-M24 each appear exactly once); (2) tracing every code path in workflow/analysis.py for a mechanism that could enter a row or unit more than once into the Fisher table (read_pots reads the file once, check_one_row_per_pot raises on duplicates, cross_tabulate increments exactly one cell per row, and build_report uses only the resulting 2x2 table); and (3) independently recomputing the tally (pelleted 9/12 emerged, bare 3/12) and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value via the hypergeometric distribution (2 * (48400 + 4356 + 144 + 1) / C(24,12) = 105802/2704156 = 0.0391) and odds ratio (9*9)/(3*3) = 9.00, which match the report exactly and would not match if any unit had been double-counted. All three attempts failed to produce evidence of repeated independent-unit entry.
